title: Reading Without a Reader: Large Language Models Collapse Reading and Writing into a Single Entangled Code

images.desc:
4.2 Written language as an acquired cultural overlay


A from-scratch transformer has no evolved substrate for orthography; any
sensitivity to legal letter sequences must be acquired. Using the aligned
Pythia checkpoints, we measure an orthographic word-form gap, defined as
bpb​(illegal)−bpb​(real)\mathrm{bpb}(\text{illegal})-\mathrm{bpb}(\text{real}) over the continuation tokens of a word
form (carrier masked), ordered real << legal-pseudoword << illegal at every
checkpoint. The raw gap is dominated by a tokenization confound (illegal
consonant strings fragment into many more BPE sub-tokens than real words), so for
pythia-160m it is already large at random initialization (5.885.88 bits/byte) and,
if anything, shrinks as the model learns to compress all three classes
(to 4.384.38 at the final checkpoint). The genuine, acquired signal appears only
once this confound is removed: the token-count–residualized gap grows
over training from 1.481.48 to 1.851.85 bits/byte, and a token-count–matched subset
grows from 2.932.93 to 3.803.80 (Table B2;
Figure 1). Orthographic word-form selectivity is therefore
acquired over training, as the neuronal-recycling framing predicts for a cultural
skill, though we cannot fully exclude residual subword-frequency structure. We do
not claim a clean co-onset with the induction phase change: the raw-gap
onset is itself a tokenization artifact (its maximum-slope step is step 1), and,
as we show next, the induction circuit is causally unrelated to the gap. We thus
report the controlled word-form gap as a gradually acquired code rather
than one temporally locked to circuit emergence.


We confirm the same orthographic distinction directly. A linear probe
separates real/legal/illegal word forms with 0.9330.933 three-class accuracy at
pythia-160m’s best layer (layer 8), well above both chance (0.3330.333) and a
permutation null (0.3520.352), and a token-count–matched real-vs-scrambled
control (0.8690.869) rules out token-count leakage
(Table B3). Decodability peaks in mid-to-late layers, the
“letterbox” depth profile (Figure 2).


Critically, this orthographic code is not carried by the induction
circuit. Ablating the top induction head (L4H6 in pythia-160m) leaves the
word-form gap essentially intact: it moves from a clean 4.3244.324 to 4.3614.361
under ablation, a fraction remaining of 1.0091.009 (a matched random-head control
shifts the gap by only −0.001-0.001; the gap does not collapse). This is an honest
negative: the mechanism that supports in-context copying (Section 4.1)
is dissociable from the one that encodes orthographic legality. We emphasize
that the analogy to the visual word form area and neuronal recycling
(Dehaene and Cohen, 2007, 2011; Morais et al., 1979) is to acquisition
timing only; a randomly initialized transformer has no pre-existing evolved
cortex to recycle.


Figure 1: Orthographic word-form gap (bpb​(illegal)−bpb​(real)\mathrm{bpb}(\text{illegal})-\mathrm{bpb}(\text{real}))
over Pythia training. The raw gap (dominated by a BPE tokenization confound) is
large at initialization and shrinks; the token-count–controlled gap, the
genuine acquired signal, grows with tokens seen.


Figure 2: Layerwise linear-probe decodability of word-form class. Decodability
peaks in mid-to-late layers above the permutation null.

4.3 The data cost of competence


Both loss and grammaticality improve smoothly as a function of tokens seen
(Table LABEL:tab:exp3_data_dynamics; Figure 3). For
pythia-160m, perplexity on held-out text falls from ∼\sim6.3×1046.3\times 10^{4} at
step 1 to ∼\sim5050 at the final checkpoint, while BLiMP grammaticality rises
from chance (0.4840.484) to 0.7440.744; the larger pythia-410m reaches 0.8050.805. An
across-size loss-vs-NN power law at the final checkpoint has exponent
αN=0.100\alpha_{N}=0.100 (with the within-run fits flagged as autocorrelated, so their
intervals understate uncertainty). The machine reaches this competence only
after ∼\sim3×10113\times 10^{11} tokens (∼\sim2.3×10112.3\times 10^{11} word-equivalents
assuming a nominal 1.31.3 tokens/word), three to four orders of magnitude beyond the
∼\sim100M-word budget a child has by age 13 (band 50–200M words, i.e. 65–260M tokens; Warstadt et al., 2023). We treat the human comparison as
illustrative and order-of-magnitude only: children receive multimodal,
embodied, interactive, child-directed input, whereas the Pile is adult written
text, so this is not a confirmed cognitive equivalence
(Lake et al., 2017; Chollet, 2019; Spelke and Kinzler, 2007).


Figure 3: Loss vs tokens seen on released Pythia checkpoints. Competence
arrives only after ∼\sim101110^{11} tokens.

4.4 Form before meaning


Across the Pythia scale ladder, formal competence (BLiMP grammaticality)
exceeds and saturates ahead of functional competence
(Table B5; Figure 4). At the top of
our ladder, pythia-1.4b reaches BLiMP 0.8240.824 [0.8070.807, 0.8410.841] while its
functional composite (the mean of the PIQA physical-commonsense,
situation-tracking, and absurdity-detection accuracies) reaches
0.7570.757, a form−-function gap of 0.0670.067. Form rises early and plateaus;
function lags and remains below it. These results hold under a
difficulty/length-matched control and a PPMI surface baseline, following the
formal/functional distinction of Mahowald et al. (2024); Fedorenko et al. (2024). We
are candid that the gap is modest at 1.4b, that the situation-tracking items are
author-made and templated (frozen across runs), and that there is no human
ceiling; the claim is scoped to these probes, not to meaning in general
(Bender and Koller, 2020; Harnad, 1990).


Figure 4: Formal (BLiMP) vs functional competence across the Pythia scale
ladder. Form leads and saturates; function lags.

Null: no evidence that compression decouples from reasoning.


We
tested whether better compression and better functional competence
dissociate across scale. We find no evidence for decoupling: across the
six Pythia sizes the point estimate runs in the opposite direction
(bits/byte vs functional composite Pearson r=−0.68r=-0.68, p=0.14p=0.14; Spearman
ρ=−0.66\rho=-0.66, p=0.16p=0.16; n=6n=6; Figure 6), i.e. if
anything the two improve together. With n=6n=6 this is underpowered and cannot
establish co-variation either; the only safe conclusion is that the
“compression decoupled from reasoning” hypothesis is not supported, and
we withdraw it as a positive claim.


Figure 5: Bits/byte vs non-embedding parameters: a clean power law
(α=0.090\alpha=0.090 [0.0800.080, 0.1070.107], R2=0.984R^{2}=0.984).


Figure 6: Compression (bits/byte) vs functional competence across six sizes.
The point estimate runs opposite to decoupling (Pearson r=−0.68r=-0.68, p=0.14p=0.14,
n=6n=6); underpowered, but the decoupling hypothesis is not supported.

4.6 A knowledge repository against a grounding ceiling


Three separate probes characterize the model as a text repository operating
against a distributional ceiling; we report them separately rather than merged
(Table B9). First, extractable verbatim memorization of
Pile text grows log-linearly with scale, with slope 0.0110.011 [0.0070.007, 0.0170.017]
in log\log non-embedding parameters (R2≈0.63R^{2}\approx 0.63), against a non-member
negative control (Figure 7), consistent with prior
memorization laws (Carlini et al., 2023, 2021). Second,
on three-choice tool-use items, the imitation−-innovation gap reaches 0.0900.090
while a PPMI rarity baseline reproduces a gap of 0.0000.000, so the innovation
deficit is not explained by option rarity (Yiu et al., 2024). Third, on a
bounded symbol-grounding demonstration, hidden-state geometry tracks perceptual
size norms with |ρ||\rho| up to 0.830.83 (rising with scale), beating a PPMI
baseline (|ρ||\rho| max 0.510.51), whereas for lightness the model does
not beat the PPMI baseline (Figure 8;
Harnad, 1990; Bisk et al., 2020). The three probes measure
different constructs, and “repository, not abstraction” is a hypothesis, not
proven by any single one.


Figure 7: Verbatim Pile extraction grows log-linearly with non-embedding
parameters (slope 0.0110.011 [0.0070.007, 0.0170.017]).


Figure 8: Hidden-state geometry vs perceptual norms against a PPMI baseline.
Size is captured above the baseline; lightness is not.

Null: no entanglement trend with scale.


Across the six untied
sizes, ℰ\mathcal{E} does not vary systematically with model size: Spearman(ℰ,log⁡N)=0.37(\mathcal{E},\log N)=0.37 (permutation p=0.49p=0.49, n=6n=6; Appendix Figure A3). We
report this as a flat, underpowered null rather than a trend.


Figure 9: Entanglement index ℰ\mathcal{E} by architecture. Tied models sit at
1.01.0 by construction; untied Pythia models sit at 0.230.23–0.350.35, far above
the independent-init floor.
